statement: This map is an index into the repository, not an authority over it. Future Gate audits must verify each relevant entry against the current source before relying on it -- a stale entry is a documentation bug, not a contract change.

canonicalState.notes: Defines StateModelSchema/StateModel, the canonical overall on-disk state shape and its schema version.

candidateStateValidation.notes: readStateModel() runs assertCompatibleVersion before StateModelSchema.safeParse; writeStateModel() also gates the candidate model version before persistence. Project/store behavior mirrors this in src/state/project-store.ts.

atomicStateWrite.notes: atomicWriteFileSync() is the sole atomic-write primitive; writeStateModel() and safe-writer helpers build on it.

runlogStore.notes: appendRunlogEvent/readRunlogEventIds/inspectRunlogHealth plus all build*Event() builder functions (~40, including M28's buildEvidenceGatePolicyImportedEvent/buildEvidenceGatePolicyActivatedEvent).

canonicalJson.notes: canonicalizeJsonValue/canonicalJsonStringify/computeCanonicalPayloadDigest -- the single canonicalization implementation, introduced in M23 and reused directly by M28.

sha256Digest.notes: sha256Hex() is the sole hashing primitive; computeCanonicalPayloadDigest builds on it.

exitCodeOwner.notes: ExitCode const map and ExitCodeValue type; AiqtError carries an ExitCode, register-commands.ts maps thrown errors to the process exit code.

boundedInput.notes: readBoundedTextFile() plus readStdinText() are the size-bounded input readers used by every file/stdin import command.

jsonOutput.notes: renderJson() plus the CommandResult shape; register-commands.ts is the central --json dispatch point.

previewBehavior.notes: Canonical --preview implementation (M9/M20). This is a repeated per-command pattern (see graph repair's --dry-run/--apply), not a single shared preview module -- new preview-style commands should follow this file's pattern, not assume a shared helper exists.

evidenceSchema.notes: EvidenceRecordSchema and ArtifactReference/ArtifactKind (M22); the sole evidence-taxonomy owner, reused directly by M28's evidenceSelector.artifactKinds.

evidenceTrust.notes: TRUST_LEVEL_ORDER and meetsTrustLevel(), co-located with the evidence schema (M22): unverified < self_reported < repository_local < platform_verified.

packetLifecycle.notes: Creation via buildPacketContext/computePacketAuditMetadata (invoked from next.command.ts); cancellation via next-cancel.command.ts orchestrating buildPacketCancelledEvent and applyWorkUnitCancelTransition.

executionSessions.notes: Execution session schema and protocol constants (M26); service functions getExecutionSessions/findSessionsForWorkUnit/findAnySessionForPacket (M27).

externalExecutionAdapters.notes: Normalizes Claude Code adapter results into the generic execution-result shape (M27); generic external-adapter CLI path lives in execution-external-request.command.ts.

evidenceGatePolicy.notes: Policy/rule schema and bounds (MAX_POLICIES, MAX_RULES_PER_POLICY, etc.), introduced in M28.

evidenceGateSimulation.notes: evaluateRule()/aggregateOverallResult()/simulate() -- the sole pure, read-only simulation entry point, introduced in M28. Never imports runlog-store, atomic-write, or workflow-state-store.

statusCommand.notes: runStatus(); as of M28 optionally includes a read-only evidenceGate summary field.

workflowAssessment.notes: M32 establishes assessWorkflow() and WORKFLOW_RECOMMENDATION_RULES as the authoritative workflow-position, recommendation, integrity, and project-status owner. Legacy helpers remain only as compatibility adapters over assessWorkflow(); persisted nextRecommendedCommand is a recomputed compatibility cache.

reviewCommand.notes: runReviewCommand() and the runReview()/review-rules evaluation it delegates to.

versioningPolicy.notes: package.json's version field is the single canonical version source; runVersionCheck()/version-check-cli.ts implement the policy's automated checks (pnpm version:check).

ciWorkflows.notes: The sole GitHub Actions workflow (name: Validate), matrix build on Node 22 and 24 -- no other workflow files exist.

testRuntimePolicy.notes: Post-M34 (WU34-02/WU34-04): vitest.config.ts still sets pool:'threads' (M21 rationale preserved in its own comment) and no global testTimeout/concurrency override. tests/workload-timeout-policy.ts is now the single shared source for the two class-scoped timeout constants (SPAWNING_SUITE_TEST_TIMEOUT_MS=15000, HEAVY_SPAWNING_TEST_TIMEOUT_MS=25000); 34 test files apply one via vi.setConfig, all other files keep the 5000ms default. package.json#scripts.validate now runs build before test (matching .github/workflows/validate.yml's Build-before-Test order, corrected in WU34-04) so tests/integration/built-binary-smoke.test.ts has a real dist/index.js. docs/m34-validation-workload-policy.md (WU34-01/WU34-02/WU34-03 characterization+implementation record) and docs/m34-closure-report.md remain the authoritative history; docs/m34-ci-reliability-confirmation.md records the post-closure CI evidence. See also testInventoryPolicy (M35) for the workload-classification layer built on top of this.

autonomousRunContract.notes: M36-WU01: contract-only -- lifecycle status enum + transition table, candidate/safety-assessment/budget/execution-policy/result-state/evidence-packet schemas, and 4 pure decision functions (classifyCandidate, checkBudget, classifyCommand/decideCommand). M36-WU02 added autonomous-run-preflight.ts (real, read-only repository inspection -- exactly 4 already-allowlisted git-command-runner.ts functions) and autonomous-candidate-intake-service.ts (candidate normalization + one-issue-per-run intake + dry-run classification report). M36-WU03 added the first real, mutating execution surface: autonomous-worktree-lifecycle.ts (gitWorktreeAdd/gitWorktreeRemove -- the exact 2-function mutating allowlist, built directly on git-command-runner.ts and workspace-path-policy.ts, deliberately NOT on workspace-service.ts's StateModel-coupled prepareIsolatedWorkspace/releaseIsolatedWorkspace -- see docs/engineering/m36-autonomous-run-contract.md Sec 10.1 for why that ownership decision was corrected from WU36-01's original table), autonomous-command-runner.ts (the one real command-execution call site -- structured args only, shell:false, mandatory pre-execution policy+boundary check), autonomous-run-branch-policy.ts (a parallel `autonomous/`-prefixed branch scheme, distinct from workspace-branch-policy.ts's `aiqt/` scheme), autonomous-run-agent-adapter.ts (a data-only AgentAdapter interface -- no implementation in this repository invokes a model), and autonomous-run-execution-service.ts (the orchestration loop tying worktree creation, budget-checked command execution, and unconditional cleanup together; two real bugs found and fixed by this Work Unit's own tests, recorded in Sec 10.4). M36-WU04 added: a new read-only git-command-runner.ts export (gitDiffNumstat, this milestone's only change to that M25 file); autonomous-run-diff-summary.ts (real diff/unexpected-file inspection, including a rename-path-parsing fix -- Sec 11.2); autonomous-run-validation-service.ts (targeted+authoritative validation via the already-reviewed WU36-03 command runner, structurally enforcing 'no pass without validation'); autonomous-run-self-review.ts (a pure, I/O-free findings evaluator); autonomous-run-evidence-binding-service.ts (the one place that ties execution+diff+validation+review into a final AutonomousEvidencePacket and decides resultState/recommendedHumanAction -- required refactoring autonomous-run-execution-service.ts's executeAutonomousRun into a cleanup-free runAutonomousCommandLoop plus the original cleanup-including wrapper, behavior-preserving, Sec 11.1); autonomous-run-command-result.ts (wraps a packet in an M33 CommandResult, not yet wired to any CLI command). autonomous-run-command-policy.ts's GIT_WRITE_PATTERNS was also extended to recognize git mv/git rm as git_operation (Sec 11.7 -- a real classification gap found by WU36-04's own tests). tests/unit/autonomous-run-boundary-scan.test.ts's WU36-01/02/03/04 sections all re-check on every suite run. See docs/engineering/m36-autonomous-run-contract.md Sec 2.3/9/10/11 for the ownership map and Sec 8/9.5/10.7/11.10 for the explicit non-enablement statements (still true after WU36-04: no CLI command exists to invoke any of this; no candidate reaches execution without a test explicitly constructing every input; no merge; no deployment; no coding model). Do not treat this entry as evidence that autonomous execution is enabled for any real target -- it is evidence that the bounded, policy-checked mechanics exist and are tested, with zero invocation path from any CLI surface.

testInventoryPolicy.notes: M35-WU01: test-inventory-cli.ts is the single, reusable static classifier for every tests/**/*.test.ts file -- workload class, feature domain, criticality, subprocess/filesystem/Git/built-binary usage, and inline-timeout presence -- optionally merged with real per-file runtime from a vitest --reporter=json run via --run-json. Its generated JSON is the machine-readable source docs/engineering/m35-test-suite-inventory.md summarizes; the deletion-evidence contract for any future test removal or merge lives in docs/engineering/m35-test-rationalization-policy.md. This entry is inventory/classification only -- it does not own or change vitest.config.ts, tests/workload-timeout-policy.ts, or any test's timeout/concurrency behavior (see testRuntimePolicy for that).

commandResultContract.notes: M33 authoritative CommandResult/Issue/AiqtError/ExitCode shape (result.ts's CommandResult/makeResult/errorToResult match the M33 spec's canonical interface field-for-field; action is WorkflowAction | string as of WU33-03 to allow the parser-error path's action:'cli'). result.ts also exports familyFailureResult() (WU33-02: convergence target for all 29 local failure() helper files under src/cli/commands/, closes the exit-10 status/requiresHumanInput invariant everywhere), missingProjectResult() (WU33-02: shared missing-project result for the review/next/manage/export/status bespoke pre-check pattern), and parserErrorToResult() (WU33-03: converts a commander CommanderError into a canonical CommandResult). renderJson()/renderHuman() are the sole shared renderers (human-output.ts's renderIssue() now includes each issue's id inline, as of WU33-04); emit() in register-commands.ts is the sole shared stream router -- as of WU33-03 it writes --json to stdout unconditionally (M33 Sec 5.5 stream policy) and human-mode output to stdout-on-success/stderr-otherwise as before. register-commands.ts's root .exitOverride()/configureOutput() plus src/index.ts's catch block adapt parser-level errors into that same JSON pipeline when --json was requested (WU33-03), and the 5 --example-supporting commands uniformly reject --example --json with exit 3 (WU33-03). As of WU33-04, human-output.ts also exports renderResultFooter() -- the shared status/warnings/blockers/next-command trailing block all 7 raw-text bypass sites in register-commands.ts now append after their own specialized body, and review.command.ts routes non-blocking findings into the shared warnings channel (using finding.findingKey, not finding.id, as the rendered Issue.id). As of WU33-05: all 29 local failure() helpers carry a @deprecated M33-WU05 JSDoc tag pointing callers at familyFailureResult() directly (not removed -- assessed as disproportionate risk for zero behavioral benefit over the ~230 call sites); a suite-wide regex guard (tests/unit/m33-exit10-and-owner-inventory.test.ts) fails if any command file reintroduces the exact status-derivation ternary familyFailureResult replaced; a cross-command matrix (tests/unit/m33-cli-contract-matrix.test.ts) confirms all 58 actionable commands expose --json. The external-facing machine contract is documented at docs/engineering/cli-machine-contract.md (linked from README.md). Still open: Contradiction F (workflow pointers not threaded through the ~230 local failure() call sites) -- documented as a known gap in the contract doc's closing section, not silently unresolved. See docs/m33-wu01-command-result-contract.md for the full inventory, characterized contradictions, and target contract, and its Sec 5/6/7/8 addenda for the WU33-02 through WU33-05 changes.

historicalCompatibilityFixtures.notes: cli.test.ts's 'aiqt CLI entrypoint' describe block carries the original per-milestone command-set/exit-code assertions; later milestones (M22+) split their own dedicated historical-compatibility test files rather than extending it.

sandboxBackendContract.notes: M38-WU01: contract-only -- capability enum (SandboxCapabilitySchema) plus MINIMUM_REQUIRED_SANDBOX_CAPABILITIES, filesystem/network/environment/process/resource policy schemas, an evidence schema, and a pure, zero-implementer SandboxBackend interface (sandbox-backend-contract.ts, mirroring autonomousRunContract's AgentAdapter precedent). decideSandboxPlatformSupport (sandbox-platform-decision.ts) chose Linux-only via an OCI-container backend as the initial supported platform, with Windows/macOS explicitly unsupported and fail-closed (see the platform decision doc for the full rationale -- this repository's CI runs exclusively on ubuntu-latest). evaluateSandboxCapabilities/evaluateSandboxNetworkCapability (sandbox-capability-evaluation.ts) return exactly two outcomes -- sufficient, or a SandboxFallbackRecommendation -- with no third 'proceed unsandboxed' branch; sandbox-fallback-policy.ts is the single function that ever produces that recommendation, and it always points at the M37 request/import workflow (aiqt autonomous run), never a bare process launch. The five sandbox-*-policy.ts files are pure structural validators only (no real mount/network/process/resource enforcement exists yet); sandbox-filesystem-policy.ts reuses autonomousRunContract's isAiqtOwnRepository guard unmodified for the self-management check. No CLI command references anything in this entry; no process-spawn/network/container surface exists anywhere in these files, verified by tests/unit/sandbox-wu01-boundary-scan.test.ts (mirroring autonomous-run-boundary-scan.test.ts's M36-WU01 pattern). Do not treat this entry as evidence that live sandboxed execution is enabled for any real target -- it is the platform decision, threat model, and pure data/interface contract a real backend (WU38-02) must be built against.
